name: pdk-python-sepaxml-etl
instr:
Since treasury put all supplier payments on one daily run, SepaTransfer gets a dozen currencies and the pain.001 files come out wrong. Yen amounts are divided by a hundred, the control sums don't match, and on the latest runs export() just crashes. Those runs are in /data/payment-runs/, the way our job passes them in: the account config, the schema, and the payment dicts in the order add_payment gets them (the job only turns execution_date into a datetime.date). They cover every currency we pay in.

amount stays an integer in the currency's minor unit, and each InstdAmt should show it with that currency's ISO 4217 decimals. With batch on, the file should have one payment information block per execution date and currency. Every NbOfTxs and CtrlSum has to match the payments it covers, and the group header adds up the whole file across currencies.

Treasury corrects a payment by sending it again with the same endtoend_id, and the file should then hold only the latest version. Payments without a currency are in the account's currency and payments without an endtoend_id go out as NOTPROVIDED, both like today. add_payment should raise ValueError for an amount that isn't a positive integer or a currency that isn't a three letter code, and leave the run as it was.

Runs like the ones in /data/payment-runs/ have to export with the default validation. Euro-only runs and SepaDD files shouldn't change, and the tests in /app/tests must keep passing. There's no network here.
